newsitem.title: USA: Govs ask US budget panels for transportation funds.
newsitem.headline: Govs ask US budget panels for transportation funds.

text.p: The nation's governors called on the U.S. Congress on Friday to release more transportation trust fund dollars "to meet critical transportation needs in every state."
"We cannot afford not to invest in transportion," 51 governors, including the governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, said in a letter to House and Senate budget panels.
"Transportation is vital to economic growth, job creation and service delivery," they said in the letter coordinated by the National Governors' Association (NGA).
NGA said in a press statement that budget negotiators recently got a transportation spending windfall because of a projected increase in tax receipts stemming from the healthy U.S. economy.
But the governors warned budget leaders that the economic prosperity could be "seriously hampered" if Congress does not invest in the "nation's transportation future."
"The budget deal hinges on solid economic growth throughout the nation, yet our crumbling infrastructure stands to dramatically impede that growth," the governors said.
The governors warned that federal investment in transportation is declining at a time when revenues generated through a tax on motorists will rise sharply - by more than 15 percent through 2002.

Administration studies show that annual transportation funds from all levels of government would need to be increased by $18.2 billion - more than 40 percent - simply to maintain current highway, bridge and transit conditions, governors said.
